signals.title: NZD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Divergence
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard registers an extreme divergence between NZD and NOK over the 1-week window. NZD leads the G10 complex with an average gain of +0.842% across 4 pairs, while NOK lags at -0.979% across 2 pairs, generating a 1.822% bilateral spread. Crude oil dropped sharply with WTI down -4.49% to $86.8 intraday following reports of easing Strait of Hormuz naval tensions, directly eroding terms-of-trade support for the petroleum-linked Norwegian krone. Despite the RBNZ policy rate sitting at 2.75% against Norges Bank's 4.5%—a 175bp nominal carry disadvantage for the kiwi—spot NZD/USD gained +1.53% intraday to 0.5632 while USD/NOK trades above its 20-day average at 9.393. The broad rebound in risk sentiment, marked by the S&P 500 rallying +2.35% and VIX dropping -22.31% to 19.9, favors high-beta cyclical currencies over European petro-currencies in the near term. Trade bias: Long NZD/NOK; wide G10 momentum spread and crude collapse favor NZD outperformance. Catalyst: Norges Bank Financial Stability Report on 10 Nov at 07:30 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz transit disruptions resume or crude rebounds above $90, reversing NOK weakness.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Elevated Vol Premium + Downside Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.89, holding below its SMA20 at 157.93 and SMA200 at 158.66 within a tight 20-session range. Implied volatility trades at 6.7% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, leaving an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.0% that signals persistent demand for options protection. The 25-delta Risk Reversal prints at -2.05, demonstrating a heavy put skew as market participants price downside protection despite a 269bp OIS carry advantage favoring the dollar (SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23%). CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY by -21,213 contracts at the 92nd percentile of its 52-week range, creating unwind vulnerability if domestic monetary policy tightens. With 160.00 remaining the key level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention, options markets are hedging spot pullbacks rather than chasing carry extension. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY; elevated options put skew caps upside above the 200-day moving average. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions on 9 Nov at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Sustained breakout above 158.66 invalidates the topping structure and targets the 160.00 intervention watch level.
evidence: USD/JPY OIS carry: SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23% (+269bp)

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short vs Rates Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1227, closing above its SMA20 of 1.1198 while remaining capped beneath the falling SMA50 at 1.1339. CFTC Leveraged Funds net positioning stands at -104,030 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.80, confirming a stretched institutional short. This crowded short faces diminishing fundamental momentum as 2Y sovereign yield spreads narrowed 22bp in EUR's favor over the trailing 20 sessions to -160bp, even as the Fed at 4.00% maintains a 135bp policy advantage at 2.65%. While ESTR at 2.44% vs SOFR at 3.92% yields a +148bp carry spread backing the dollar, US 5Y yields fell 44bp over the past 20 sessions led by a 33bp decline in real yields (FRED, as of Nov 5). An extreme short position combined with narrowing real yield support leaves EUR/USD primed for short-covering squirts toward the 50-day moving average. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD; crowded spec short positioning creates asymmetric upside covering risk. Catalyst: Germany CPI at 07:00 UTC followed by US CPI at 13:30 UTC on 10 Nov. Risk: US Core CPI prints above the 0.2% consensus, re-widening the short-end rate gap in favor of USD.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Breakout + Speculative Add
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3443, executing a technical breakout above its SMA20 (1.336), SMA50 (1.336), and SMA200 (1.342) cluster with a wide-range bar measuring 2.3 times its 10-bar average body. Institutional positioning aggressively supports the move, with CFTC Leveraged Funds expanding net longs by +12,670 contracts WoW to +32,686 contracts (65th percentile). Cash rate differentials sit flat with the BoE at 4.00% matching the Fed at 4.00%, while OIS pricing yields a negligible 19bp SOFR premium over SONIA at 3.73%. UK 10Y Gilt yields trade at 5.16% (+28bp over US Treasuries at 4.88%), providing structural sovereign yield backing to the pound. With the options market reflecting a neutral stance via a mild 25d Risk Reversal of -0.42, spot price structure exhibits higher swing highs and lows that confirm short-term trend continuation. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD; spot clearance above the moving-average cluster confirms trend momentum. Catalyst: BoE MPC Member Pill speech on 10 Nov at 18:30 UTC. Risk: Daily close below the SMA200 anchor at 1.3420 negates the breakout structure.

supports: technical regime points with the stated direction
